chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “When an event occurs to the Imam عليه السلام, how should the people act?” He عليه السلام said: “Where is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?”
“Why should not, then, a group from every party among them go forth, so that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious?”
He عليه السلام said: “They are excused as long as they are engaged in seeking, and those who are waiting for them are also excused until their companions return to them.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابُهُمْ: their companions who return with the needed knowledge
key_terms.الدِّينِ: the religion, meaning the body of divine guidance and belief
key_terms.الطَّلَبِ: the process of seeking and investigating the truth
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely appointed Imam whose passing raises the question of succession
key_terms.حَدَثٌ: an event, here referring to the occurrence of death or a major occurrence affecting the Imam
key_terms.فِي عُذْرٍ: being excused and not blameworthy during the period of seeking
key_terms.لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا: to gain deep understanding of the religion
key_terms.يُنْذِرُوا: to warn and inform their people with religious guidance

ai.seo_question: What are people required to do when the Imam passes away and the next Imam must be identified?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the community’s duty when an Imam عليه السلام passes away and people must identify the succeeding Imam. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام cites the Qur’anic principle of a group going forth to gain understanding and return with guidance, showing that those who seek the truth and those awaiting their report are excused during that period. The narration emphasizes religious authority, communal responsibility, and the legitimacy of seeking knowledge in times of uncertainty.
